items.desired_behavior: one event-scoped transaction covers session upsert and affected program/partition replacement; affected session IDs are derived from parsed sessions (including empty ones), not from programs; after a successful import, the imported/default session is selected and an explicit 'Open Console with [session]' action is offered.
acceptance_criteria: New event -> valid XLSX -> confirmation -> explicit session selection -> Console -> Start works without a hidden header action
when multiple sessions exist, the user must make an explicit choice — the import path never silently starts a show by guessing which session is active
session upsert and affected program/partition replacement happen inside ONE event-scoped database transaction, not two separate operations
affected session IDs are derived from the parsed SESSIONS, including empty ones — not derived from programs, so an empty imported session still replaces (clears) any stale programs on that session
authorization and tenant scope are confirmed INSIDE the database operation itself (including any SECURITY DEFINER privileges and search_path on the RPC), not only by the calling route's own guard
on failure, the client receives a generic error; protected diagnostic detail is logged server-side only, never returned raw to the client
a foreign session id (belonging to a different event) is rejected, not silently accepted
invalid, duplicate, and oversized files are all rejected with an actionable error and mutate nothing
an induced mid-operation failure (e.g. the replacement step failing after the upsert step would otherwise have committed) results in a full rollback, not a partially-committed session
refresh preserves a coherent session choice after import
any required migration is additive, verified in staging first, with a recovery plan; no production migration without separate authorization
